paper.title: EZ-STANCE: A Large Dataset for English Zero-Shot Stance Detection

source.code_commit: b53dc64ce29622dd845c933972fdfbc17a0210ba (2025-04-17, HEAD of main at download)
source.licence: None stated: the GitHub repo has no LICENSE file and the GitHub API reports license=null; the README only asks users to cite the paper. Texts are tweets (Twitter/X terms). Treated as not redistributable: the frozen files hold no tweet text or target.
source.columns_used: Text (preprocessed tweet, the column the paper's models use per README note 1), Target 1, Stance 1 (AGAINST/FAVOR/NONE); Subtask B files also carry Domain and In Use (all released test rows have In Use = 1). Ori Text (raw tweet), Keywords and seen? are not used.
source.label_order: AGAINST=0, FAVOR=1, NONE=2 (EMNLP2024_ezstance/src/utils/preprocessing.py); the paper's F1macro is the unweighted mean of these three per-class F1s (utils/evaluation.py compute_f1).
source.unused_release_parts: train/val CSVs; the prompt/ subfolders (noun-phrase targets rewritten with the paper's NLI templates for BART-MNLI-ep training); the mixed/ test files (verified to equal the union of noun_phrase/ and claim/ files, so the target type is taken from those).

splits_in_release.subtaskA: target-based ZSSD: one train/val/test split; test = noun_phrase 2,663 + claim 5,135 = mixed 7,798 (matches paper Table 5).
splits_in_release.subtaskB: domain-based ZSSD: 8 leave-one-domain-out splits; the test set of each is (almost all) data from the held-out domain. Test N (noun_phrase + claim = mixed), all matching paper Table 13: CE covid19_domain 2,639+3,819=6,458; WE world_event_domain 2,286+3,252=5,538; EdC education_and_culture_domain 2,109+3,078=5,187; EnC consumption_and_entertainment_domain 2,702+4,053=6,755; S sports_domain 1,807+2,661=4,468; R rights_domain 2,468+3,405=5,873; EP environmental_protection_domain 2,071+2,772=4,843; P politic 2,890+3,999=6,889. Total 46,011; the eight test sets are pairwise disjoint.
splits_in_release.overlap: 6,630 of the 7,798 Subtask A test pairs also occur in some Subtask B test set; requests are identical for identical (tweet, target, target type), so the Jev cache serves them once.

english_verification.paper: Appendix B: tweets were filtered to 'keep only tweets in English'; annotators' native language was English (Section 3.2). Claim targets are annotator-written English sentences.
english_verification.method: All 9,296 unique test tweets (Text) were screened: (1) langid.py 1.1.6 on the whole text (37 non-en) and on 8-token windows (non-en with p>0.999); (2) count of non-Latin-script letters >= 2; (3) two independent LLM screening passes (a general-purpose chat LLM, not Jev/TypeSafe; batches of 40, different random batching) asking for tweets containing any non-English sentence/clause/multi-word phrase, code-mixed text, or pidgin/creole/patois. The 268 candidates from the union were then judged from the text alone (no labels, no Jev outputs).
english_verification.rule: Exclude a tweet if it contains a non-English sentence, clause or multi-word phrase (including quoted/retweeted tweets, Twitter UI labels in another language, and link-preview titles), code-mixed text with non-English grammar or function words (Hinglish, Taglish, Manglish, Sheng, ...), or English-lexifier pidgin/creole/patois (Nigerian/Ghanaian Pidgin, Jamaican/Trinidadian creole), under the benchmark's English-only rule. Keep proper names in any script, handles, hashtags, single loanwords/particles (e.g. 'Aiyah', 'la', 'da'), and names of events/titles.
english_verification.result: 152 tweets excluded (hash list: data/frozen/ezstance/non_english_texts.json). Targets were not screened for exclusion: they are annotator-written; langid flags on the 40,754 unique targets are short names/phrases.

frozen.builder: scripts/prepare_ezstance.py (deterministic; re-downloads the zip if absent and asserts its SHA-256, the per-split N of paper Tables 5/13, and mixed == noun_phrase + claim)
frozen.format: JSONL, one row per test pair: id, member (CSV path in the zip), row (0-based data-row index), target_type, domain (Subtask B), gold, sha256 = SHA-256 of JSON [Text, Target 1, Stance 1] (compact separators, UTF-8). No text is stored; ezstance.py rebuilds items from the zip and checks every row hash.

data_notes: Duplicate (tweet, target, target type) keys with conflicting gold labels: 1 in the frozen Subtask A set, 11 in Subtask B. Kept as released. Any single predictor gets at most one of each pair right.
Truncation rule (frozen in ezstance.py): tweet and target each cut to 36,000 chars; the longest state is 1,279 chars, so 0 items are truncated.
deviations: Rows whose tweet contains non-English, code-mixed or pidgin/creole text are excluded under the English-only rule, so the scored N is 7,666 (Subtask A, paper 7,798) and 45,274 (Subtask B, paper 46,011); per-domain and per-target-type N are listed above. The paper's reported numbers are on the full sets.
Subtask B aggregate 'macro_f1' is the unweighted mean over the eight domains of mixed-target macro-F1; the paper reports only per-domain values (Table 8).
